The Secure Software Development Framework groups practices into four practice groups. Consider this worked case: Prepare the Organization establishes people, processes, and technology for secure development, while Respond to Vulnerabilities identifies and remediates discovered weaknesses. On screen, create a four-step horizontal pipeline labeled 'Prepare', 'Protect', 'Produce', 'Respond', with each step containing a brief icon representing its core function. Follow every arrow in order and name the state before and after each transition. The trace converts an abstract statement into an inspectable sequence.

Prepare the Organization establishes people, processes, and technology for secure development. Consider this worked case: Teams define security policies, train developers on secure coding standards, and select development environments before writing code. On screen, illustrate a checklist with three items: 'People Training', 'Process Documentation', 'Technology Configuration', each with a checkmark. Compare alternatives against the same constraints so the evaluation does not move the goalposts. Using shared criteria turns a preference into a defensible technical choice. Protect the Software prevents unauthorized access to code and development artifacts. Consider this worked case: Repositories use role-based access control, and source code repositories restrict commits to verified developers only. On screen, draw a locked vault icon with a key labeled 'Access Control' and a shield labeled 'Artifact Protection' surrounding a code repository symbol. beats.narration: Examine the tradeoffs in Produce Well-Secured Software Practice, including what improves and what becomes more difficult. Produce Well-Secured Software addresses security requirements, design, verification, and release. Consider this worked case: Developers integrate security requirements into design documents, run automated verification tests, and sign off on secure releases. On screen, show a document with sections labeled 'Security Requirements', 'Design Review', 'Verification Results', and 'Release Approval' in a sequential layout. State the benefit, the cost, and the condition under which the tradeoff is acceptable. Making the tradeoff visible prevents a local improvement from hiding a larger cost.

Respond to Vulnerabilities identifies, analyzes, remediates, and learns from discovered weaknesses. Consider this worked case: When a vulnerability scanner flags a flaw, the team patches the code, updates documentation, and trains staff on the new security protocol. On screen, create a cycle diagram with arrows connecting 'Identify', 'Analyze', 'Remediate', and 'Learn', forming a continuous improvement loop. Change one assumption at a time and observe which part of the reasoning no longer holds. The edge case reveals the boundary of the claim without discarding the useful core idea.

beats.narration: Use Cryptographic Standards and Confidentiality to diagnose a failure by separating symptoms, causes, and corrective action. Encryption supports confidentiality when keys and modes are used correctly. Consider this worked case: AES-256 encryption protects sensitive data in transit, provided symmetric keys are managed securely and the correct mode of operation is applied. On screen, display a padlock icon with a key labeled 'Key Management' and a gear labeled 'Mode of Operation' above a document labeled 'Confidential Data'. Locate the first point where observed behavior diverges from expected behavior, then test the smallest plausible cause. The diagnosis is strongest when another person can reproduce the observation and the test.

beats.narration: Connect Integrity, Authenticity, and Key Management to the earlier ideas and explain how the pieces work as one system. Message authentication and digital signatures address integrity and authenticity in different ways. Consider this worked case: Digital signatures verify that a code commit originated from an authorized developer, and key rotation ensures old cryptographic keys are securely destroyed after use. On screen, show a document with a signature stamp labeled 'Digital Signature' and a calendar icon labeled 'Key Rotation' next to a trash can labeled 'Secure Destruction'. Explain each connection explicitly and verify that information retains the same meaning across representations. The synthesis matters only if every connection remains supported by the original evidence.

beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Show a document with a signature stamp labeled 'Digital Signature' and a calendar icon labeled 'Key Rotation' next to a trash can labeled 'Secure Destruction'.

beats.narration: Finish with Modes of Operation and Side Channels as a practical checklist that can guide a new analysis. Modes of operation define how a primitive processes data larger than one block. Consider this worked case: Using CBC mode with a fixed IV compromises security, whereas GCM mode with a random nonce ensures proper data processing and protection against side-channel attacks. On screen, illustrate two data blocks being processed: one with a flawed 'Fixed IV' warning label, and another with a 'Random Nonce' shield icon, connected by a flow arrow labeled 'Mode of Operation'. For each checklist item, record the evidence, the remaining uncertainty, and the next verification step. The result is a repeatable procedure, not a conclusion that depends on memory or intuition.

Specific course details (such as prerequisites, course seminar, format, learning outcomes, assessment methods, and resource needs) will be determined by the faculty member(s) who propose a specific seminar course in this area. sources.author: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.excerpt: The Secure Software Development Framework groups practices into four practice groups. Prepare the Organization establishes people, processes, and technology for secure development. Protect the Software prevents unauthorized access to code and development artifacts. Produce Well-Secured Software addresses security requirements, design, verification, and release. Respond to Vulnerabilities identifies, analyzes, remediates, and learns from discovered weaknesses. Security requirements should be tracked throughout development. Verification provides evidence that selected practices and controls were performed. Security reasoning identifies assets, trust boundaries, threats, controls, evidence, residual risk, and responsibilities.
sources.title: NIST Secure Software Development Framework

sources.author: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.excerpt: Cryptographic standards define approved algorithms and parameters. Encryption supports confidentiality when keys and modes are used correctly. Message authentication and digital signatures address integrity and authenticity in different ways. Random number generation supports keys, nonces, and other security parameters. Key management covers generation, distribution, storage, use, rotation, revocation, and destruction. Modes of operation define how a primitive processes data larger than one block. Validation checks implementations against specified requirements. Security depends on the complete protocol and implementation, not only an algorithm name. Analysis also considers side channels and migration requirements.
